title: Answer "Set up Sales" — record your company's answers before testing

steps.do: Left menu → Sales → "Set up Sales" (tile on the Sales home).
steps.expect: Page headed "Sales — set up in a few questions" with sections: Approving a quote (it starts with "Who approves, and up to what value" — the levels, editable right here); Approving a deal as it moves stage; Other approvals in Sales; Reviewing the request before it is approved (contract review); Already set by your company's rules.
steps.observed: Headed "Sales — set up in a few questions"; "Approving a quote" starts with the level summary and "Who approves, and up to what value". There is no "Other approvals in Sales" section any more: since 13 Nov 2026 (commit "Sales approvals in one place") each approval has its own section — Approving a quote · Who approves, and up to what value · Approving a project costing · Opening a contract · Approving a deal as it moves stage · Leads — marking lost, giving to someone else, reopening · Reviewing the request before it is approved (contract review) · Already set by your company's rules.
steps.suggest: Page headed "Sales — set up in a few questions" with sections: Approving a quote (starting with the levels and "Who approves, and up to what value"); Approving a project costing; Opening a contract; Approving a deal as it moves stage; Leads — marking lost, giving to someone else, reopening; Reviewing the request before it is approved (contract review); Already set by your company's rules.

steps.expect: One line each for Leads (no approval), Deals, Project costing, Quotes and Opening a contract — each saying who approves.
steps.observed: Every subject still says who approves, but in its own section rather than a single "Other approvals in Sales": Leads ("only the person responsible marks a lead lost… a manager may reopen"), Deals ("only the stage rules above"), Project costing ("approved through the same levels as a quote of that value — never by the person who prepared it"), Quotes (under "Already set": "the levels above, in order…") and Opening a contract ("Today: two signatures…"). Leads need no approval to create.
steps.suggest: Read the sections "Approving a project costing", "Opening a contract", "Approving a deal as it moves stage" and "Leads — …". Expect: each says who approves (leads need no approval; deals only by stage rules; costing by the quote levels; contract by its signatures).

steps.do: Read "Already set by your company's rules".
steps.expect: Your approval levels are written out in sentences, including any value no level covers.
steps.observed: The level sentences now open the "Approving a quote" section (Level 1 — from ₹0 to ₹5,00,000 before tax: Branch Manager. Level 2 — above ₹5,00,000 to ₹25,00,000 before tax: Marketing Manager. Level 3 — above ₹25,00,000 before tax: Business Director. — and, when there is a gap, "Nothing above … is covered by a level"). "Already set by your company's rules" now lists the general rules: values before tax; a change to commercial terms cancels an approval; "Quotes: the levels above, in order — level 1 first… top management last"; who records the customer's answer; held customers get nothing new.
steps.suggest: Read the top of "Approving a quote": your levels are written out in sentences, including any value no level covers. "Already set by your company's rules" lists the fixed rules (before tax; changes cancel approval; top management last).

steps.do: Question "When a quote's value is not covered by any of your approval levels…" — choose "It goes to the approvers of your highest level". Question "May the person who prepared a quote approve it themselves…" — choose "Yes — when it is within their own authority". Question "When a quote needs more than one level, how do the levels approve?" — choose "One after another — level 1 first". Question "If a quote waits too long at one approval level…" — choose "After 1 day". Question "Must a man-month quote come from an approved project costing…" — choose "Yes — an approved costing first". Checklist: "Yes — show the checklist on every quote" and "Yes — every point must be ticked (or waived)". Press "Save these answers".
steps.expect: A message confirms the answers were saved. Reopen the page: every answer is still selected.
steps.observed: Message: "Saved. 7 answers changed — it applies from now on.". Reopened: all seven answers still selected.

steps.do: Left menu → Directory → Activity (or the activity log).
steps.expect: One entry "Sales answered: …" per changed answer, in the words of the question.

steps.do: Sign in as Test MktExec and open the same page.
steps.expect: Refused — only someone who may change the quotation approval rules may answer.
steps.observed: Refused: "Only someone who may change the Sales settings can answer these questions."
